renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: family_logo
  title: Family profile logo
  description: |-
    Each column is a match state of the family's profile HMM, drawn as a stack of amino acids whose height is the state's information content in bits. It answers which positions of the family are conserved and which residues are allowed there.
    How to read: tall stacks are conserved positions, often the functional or structural core of the family, and low flat stacks tolerate substitutions. The lanes under the logo show how often a state is occupied and how likely and how long insertions are, so a gappy region is a poor place to trust the alignment. Select a state to see the residue it matches in the representative structure.
    Lines and annotations: the total height of a stack is the state's relative entropy in bits, as in hmmlogo. The tile draws only residues more frequent than background, hmmlogo's above-background option. The consensus, RF and CS rows come from the profile file annotation.
    Source: http://eddylab.org/software/hmmer/Userguide.pdf
  kind: hmm_logo
  config:
    height_mode: relent_abovebg
    show_consensus: true
  roles:
    entity: entity
    position: position
    model: hmm_name
    state: hmm_position
    letter: hmm_letter
    emission: emission
    insert_prob: insert_prob
    insert_length: insert_length
    occupancy: occupancy
    consensus: consensus
    rf: rf
    cs: cs

- component: card
  id: state_information
  title: Information per state
  description: |-
    The hero number is the mean information content of the match states, in bits, and the box shows its quartiles. It answers how conserved the family is overall.
    How to read: a high mean means a tightly conserved family, and a low one a diverse family. A box with a long upper whisker means a few highly conserved positions stand out from a variable background.
    Source: http://eddylab.org/software/hmmer/Userguide.pdf
  column: info_bits
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: information per state, with its spread

- component: card
  id: state_occupancy
  title: State occupancy
  description: |-
    The hero number is the mean occupancy of the match states, the probability that a family member has a residue at the state, and the box shows its quartiles. It answers how gap-free the alignment behind the model is.
    How to read: values near one mean most members cover every state. A low tail marks states often skipped by members, such as fragment ends or variable loops.
  column: occupancy
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: state occupancy, with its spread

- component: table
  title: Profile states table
  description: |-
    Each row is a match state and an amino acid with its emission probability, letter height in bits, the state's information content, insert and delete behaviour, occupancy and the consensus annotation. It answers the exact numbers behind the logo.
    How to read: filter on one state to see which residues the model allows there, or sort by information content to list the most conserved positions.

outputs.name: Family member coverage of the HMM

renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: member_architecture
  title: Family member coverage of the model
  description: |-
    Each row is a member of a family alignment: a backbone for its sequence with a bar for the stretch that aligns to the family HMM, coloured by family. It answers whether the members cover the whole model or only part of it.
    How to read: members whose bar spans the whole backbone are full-length. A zigzag edge marks a member that starts after the first or ends before the last match state of the HMM, so it is a fragment or a truncated sequence. Many fragments suggest the family needs a closer look before building a structure or a logo from it.
    Lines and annotations: the zigzag edge is drawn from the first and last HMM state each member covers against the length of the model, with no score cut-off, since an hmmalign alignment carries no E-value.
    Source: http://eddylab.org/software/hmmer/Userguide.pdf
  kind: domain_architecture
  config:
    color_by: label
  roles:
    entity: entity
    start: ali_from
    end: ali_to
    label: label
    protein_length: protein_length
    hmm_from: hmm_from
    hmm_to: hmm_to
    hmm_length: hmm_length
    hmm_coverage: hmm_coverage

- component: card
  id: member_count
  title: Family members
  description: |-
    The hero number counts the aligned family members, and the bars rank the families with the most members. The second figure counts the distinct sequences. It answers how large the families are.
    How to read: a family with very few members gives a weak profile, so treat its logo with caution. Large families give more reliable conservation estimates.
  column: entity
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: label
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: members, by family

- component: card
  id: model_coverage
  title: Share of the model covered
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median share of the HMM that a member's alignment covers, and the box shows its quartiles. It answers how complete the members are.
    How to read: a median near one means most members are full length. A low median or a long lower whisker means many fragments, which weaken the conservation signal at the ends of the model.
  column: hmm_coverage
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: model coverage, with its spread

- component: figure
  title: Model coverage by family
  description: |-
    Each box is a family: the spread of the share of the HMM covered by its members. It answers which families are made of full-length members and which of fragments.
    How to read: a box close to one is a complete family, and a box that reaches low values holds many fragments. Open the architecture tile for the families with a low box.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the median share of the model covered of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of HMMER.
  visu_type: box
  dict_kwargs:
    x: label
    y: hmm_coverage
    color: label
    labels:
      label: Family
      hmm_coverage: Share of the model covered
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: hmm_coverage

- component: table
  title: Member coverage table
  description: |-
    Each row is a member of a family alignment with the first and last HMM state it covers, its length and the share of the model between them. It answers which sequences are fragments.
    How to read: sort by model coverage and open the lowest rows to see the truncated members.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: domain_score_scatter
  title: Domain score against model coverage
  description: |-
    Each point is a domain hit: the share of the family HMM its alignment covers on the horizontal axis and its bit score on the vertical axis, coloured by the database the family comes from. It answers which hits are both complete and confident.
    How to read: hits in the upper right cover the whole model with a high score, the reliable family assignments. Hits to the left only touch part of the model and are fragments or partial domains. A high score with low coverage can still be a true short match, so check the architecture tile.
    Lines and annotations: no cut-off is drawn. A score threshold is specific to each family, and Pfam stores gathering bit score thresholds inside each model, which hmmsearch applies only on request with its cut_ga option.
    Source: http://eddylab.org/software/hmmer/Userguide.pdf
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Share of the HMM covered
    y_title: Domain bit score
    top_n_labels: 10
  roles:
    x: hmm_coverage
    y: dom_score
    label: label
    color: source

- component: advanced_viz
  id: domain_architecture
  title: Domain architecture per protein
  description: |-
    Each row is a protein, drawn as a backbone with its domain hits placed along it and coloured by family. It answers which domains each protein carries and in what order.
    How to read: proteins with the same ordered list of families share an architecture, and the architectures view counts them. A zigzag edge marks a domain that matches only part of the family model. Hover a domain for its family, accession and independent E-value.
    Lines and annotations: the domain bar is the envelope on the sequence, the region HMMER judges the domain most probably lies in. The zigzag edge comes from the HMM start and end against the model length. No E-value cut-off is applied beyond the one set in the search.
    Source: http://eddylab.org/software/hmmer/Userguide.pdf
  kind: domain_architecture
  config:
    color_by: label
  roles:
    entity: entity
    start: start
    end: end
    label: label
    protein_length: protein_length
    hmm_from: hmm_from
    hmm_to: hmm_to
    hmm_length: hmm_length
    hmm_coverage: hmm_coverage
    evalue: i_evalue
    source: source
    description: description
    accession: accession

- component: card
  id: domain_hits
  title: Domain hits
  description: |-
    The hero number counts the domain hits, and the bars rank the databases they come from. The second figure counts the distinct proteins with a hit. It answers how much of the input the search annotates.
    How to read: a protein count far below the number of sequences searched means many sequences carry no recognised domain. Several hits per protein are normal for multi-domain proteins.
  column: entity
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: source
  top_n_count: 4
  caption: domain hits, by database
  headline: true

- component: card
  id: domain_families
  title: Distinct families
  description: |-
    The hero number counts the distinct families hit, and the bars rank the databases by how many of their families were found. The second figure counts all hits. It answers how diverse the annotation is.
    How to read: a high ratio of hits to families means a few families dominate. A flat ranking means the search reached many different families.
  column: label
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: source
  top_n_count: 4
  caption: families, by database

- component: card
  id: domain_score
  title: Domain bit score
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median bit score of a domain, and the box shows its quartiles. A bit score is the log-odds of the match against a null model of random sequence, so higher is stronger. It answers how strong the typical hit is.
    How to read: a high median means confident hits. A low median with a long lower whisker means many marginal hits, which are worth checking against their E-values.
    Source: http://eddylab.org/software/hmmer/Userguide.pdf
  column: dom_score
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: domain bit score, with its spread

- component: figure
  title: Domain score by database
  description: |-
    Each box is a database: the spread of domain bit scores of its hits. It answers whether one database gives stronger matches than another.
    How to read: scores of different databases are not directly comparable, because each uses its own models and thresholds. Compare the shapes, and look for a database whose box sits near the low end.
  visu_type: box
  dict_kwargs:
    x: source
    y: dom_score
    color: source
    labels:
      source: Database
      dom_score: Domain bit score

- component: table
  title: Domain hits table
  description: |-
    Each row is a domain hit with its protein, family, database, envelope span, E-values, bit score and how much of the HMM the alignment covers. It answers the exact numbers behind every tile.
    How to read: sort by independent E-value to list the most confident hits, and filter on a family or a database to inspect it.
